workflows.workflow_name: PC Does Not Power On / No Display
workflows.description: Safety-first hardware diagnostic workflow for desktops and laptops that fail to power on or power on with no display output.

safety_red_flags.label: Smoke, burning smell, sparks, or visible electrical/burn damage
safety_red_flags.warning_message: CRITICAL SAFETY STOP: Electrical fire or shock hazard detected. Do not attempt to power on or touch internal components.
safety_red_flags.escalation_instruction: Unplug power safely from the wall outlet if safe to do so, keep clear of the device, and escalate immediately to certified hardware repair.

safety_red_flags.label: Swollen laptop battery, bulging case, or leaking battery fluid
safety_red_flags.warning_message: CRITICAL SAFETY STOP: A swollen lithium-ion battery poses a severe fire and chemical hazard. Do not puncture, press, or charge the device.
safety_red_flags.escalation_instruction: Power off safely if possible, disconnect the charger, place in a well-ventilated area away from flammables, and escalate to certified hardware service.

safety_red_flags.label: Recent liquid spill on or inside the device
safety_red_flags.warning_message: CRITICAL SAFETY STOP: Powering on a liquid-damaged device can cause permanent short-circuit damage or electrical hazard.
safety_red_flags.escalation_instruction: Keep the device powered off and unplugged, and escalate to a certified technician for internal inspection.

steps.title: Verify External Power Source, Outlet, and Power Cable
steps.objective: Confirm that stable electrical power is actually reaching the computer or laptop charger before suspecting internal hardware failure.
instructions: Inspect the wall outlet, surge protector, and power strip (confirm the power strip switch is ON).
Test the wall outlet with a known-working device (such as a lamp or phone charger).
For desktops: verify the power cord is firmly seated and the rear PSU rocker switch (I/O) is set to 'I' (ON).
For laptops: verify the AC adapter brick cable is firmly connected and check for a charging indicator LED.
steps.expected_results: Wall outlet delivers power, cables are firmly seated, PSU switch is ON (desktop) or charger LED lights up (laptop).
safety_requirements: Never open a power supply unit (PSU) or AC power brick — internal capacitors can hold lethal voltage even when unplugged.
Do not use frayed, melted, or physically damaged power cables.

learning_content.why_this_step: External power issues (tripped surge protector, loose IEC power cord, switched-off PSU) are the most common and safest causes to rule out first before assuming motherboard or PSU failure.
learning_content.technical_principle: Desktop PSUs have a physical master switch (I = On, O = Off) and internal protection circuits. Laptops require correct wattage from their AC adapter to charge a deeply depleted battery.
learning_content.limitations: Confirming the wall outlet works does not guarantee the internal PSU or laptop DC-in board is delivering clean DC voltages to the motherboard.

outcomes.label: Outlet, power cable, and PSU switch / charger are verified good, but issue persists
rules_out: Dead wall outlet or turned-off surge protector
Unplugged power cord or desktop PSU switch set to Off

transition.summary: External power confirmed. Proceed to observe power button response, LEDs, fans, and beep codes.

outcomes.label: Outlet/cable/switch issue found and corrected; computer now powers on normally
outcomes.finding_hint: External power delivery interruption (loose cable, switched-off PSU, or faulty power strip) prevented startup.

transition.summary: Issue resolved after restoring external power connection.

outcomes.label: Power cord or AC adapter is physically damaged or known-good outlet shows no charger response
outcomes.finding_hint: Evidence-supported faulty or damaged external power cable / AC adapter.

transition.summary: Do not use damaged cables. Escalate for replacement certified power cable or AC adapter.

inconclusive.summary: Confirm whether the outlet was tested with another known-working device.

not_performed.summary: Workflow paused pending external power source check.

unable_to_perform.summary: Unable to verify external power safely; escalate to on-site IT support.

steps.title: Observe Power Button Response (LEDs, Fans, and POST Signals)
steps.objective: Distinguish between a 'No Power' condition (completely dead) and a 'Power On, No Display / No POST' condition.
instructions: Press the power button once firmly and observe the system for 10-15 seconds.
Note whether power/keyboard LEDs light up, whether CPU/case fans spin, and whether any motherboard beep codes or diagnostic LEDs appear.
steps.expected_results: Power LED illuminates, fans spin steadily, and the monitor displays the BIOS/UEFI splash screen.
safety_requirements: Keep the computer case closed during powered-on observation. Never touch internal components while power is connected.

learning_content.why_this_step: Separating 'No Power' from 'No Display / No POST' immediately narrows the fault domain: No Power points to PSU/battery/motherboard power delivery, whereas fans spinning with no display points to display path, GPU, or RAM/POST.
learning_content.technical_principle: During startup, the PSU sends a 'Power Good' signal to the motherboard, which then runs POST (Power-On Self-Test) to initialize CPU, RAM, and video output. Failures during POST often trigger beep codes or diagnostic LEDs.
learning_content.limitations: Spinning fans alone do not prove the PSU is outputting all required voltage rails (3.3V, 5V, 12V) within specification.

outcomes.label: Completely dead: no LEDs, no fans, and no sounds at all
rules_out: Monitor or display cable fault (system is not powering on)
outcomes.finding_hint: No power response observed despite verified wall outlet.

transition.summary: System shows no power response. Perform a safe residual power drain.

outcomes.label: Power LED lights up and/or fans spin, but the screen stays completely black
outcomes.finding_hint: System receives power (fans/LEDs active) but produces no video output.

transition.summary: Power is present without display. Proceed to verify monitor, input source, and display cable.

outcomes.label: Motherboard emits repeated beep codes or a red/amber diagnostic LED (CPU/DRAM/VGA/BOOT) stays lit
outcomes.finding_hint: Evidence-supported POST hardware fault signaled by motherboard beep codes or debug LEDs.

transition.summary: Record the exact beep pattern or LED label (CPU/DRAM/VGA) and escalate to L2/Hardware Support for ESD-safe component testing.

outcomes.label: System powers on and displays the BIOS/OS screen normally
outcomes.finding_hint: Hardware powers on and passes POST normally; if OS fails to load, switch to OS diagnostics.

transition.summary: Hardware power and display verified normal.

inconclusive.summary: Clarify whether any lights, fans, or sounds occur when pressing the power button.

not_performed.summary: Workflow paused pending power button observation.

unable_to_perform.summary: Unable to test power button safely; escalate to hardware support.

steps.title: Perform Safe Residual Power Drain (Hard Reset)
steps.objective: Discharge residual static charge from motherboard capacitors and reset latched PSU/EC protection circuits.
instructions: Ensure the computer is completely powered off.
Unplug the power cable (and disconnect all USB peripherals, docking stations, and external monitors).
Press and hold the power button for 15-20 seconds to drain residual charge.
Reconnect ONLY the power cable (no extra peripherals) and press the power button once.
steps.expected_results: Power protection resets and the computer powers on normally.
safety_requirements: Disconnect the power cable from the wall/device BEFORE holding the power button.
Do NOT disassemble laptops with sealed internal batteries or open desktop power supply units.
Ground yourself to avoid electrostatic discharge (ESD) when handling external connectors.

learning_content.why_this_step: Power surges or faulty USB peripherals can trip over-current protection in a laptop's Embedded Controller (EC) or desktop PSU. Draining residual capacitor charge resets these protection latches without opening the case.
learning_content.technical_principle: Capacitors retain small charges after unplugging. Holding the power button while disconnected discharges the standby power rails and clears transient EC/CMOS power states.
learning_content.limitations: Cannot fix failed internal PSUs, blown motherboard fuses, or dead internal batteries.

outcomes.label: Computer powers on normally after the residual power drain
rules_out: Permanent PSU or motherboard power failure
outcomes.finding_hint: Transient power protection latch or faulty external peripheral prevented power-on; resolved by residual power drain.

transition.summary: Power restored after hard reset. Reconnect peripherals one by one to check if a specific peripheral triggers the fault.

outcomes.label: Computer still shows zero signs of power after residual drain
outcomes.finding_hint: Evidence-supported internal power delivery failure (suspected PSU, power button switch, DC jack, or motherboard).

transition.summary: Escalate to certified hardware technician for PSU tester / multimeter bench diagnostics. Do not open the PSU.

inconclusive.summary: Confirm the power cord and all USB devices were disconnected during the 15-second hold.

not_performed.summary: Workflow paused pending residual power drain.

unable_to_perform.summary: Unable to perform power drain safely; escalate to hardware support.

steps.title: Verify Monitor Power, Input Source, and Video Cable
steps.objective: Confirm that the monitor itself is powered on, set to the matching input channel, and connected to the correct video port.
instructions: Check that the monitor power LED is on and press the monitor's Menu/OSD button to confirm the screen backlight works.
Verify the monitor's Input Source (HDMI 1, HDMI 2, DisplayPort, USB-C) matches the plugged-in cable.
Confirm the display cable is firmly seated at both ends.
For desktops with a dedicated graphics card (GPU): ensure the monitor is plugged into the lower GPU ports, not the motherboard onboard port.
steps.expected_results: Monitor OSD menu is visible, input source matches the cable, and video signal appears.
safety_requirements: Do not force HDMI/DisplayPort connectors into the wrong port; press the release latch on DisplayPort cables before unplugging.

learning_content.why_this_step: Many 'No Display' tickets are actually monitor input mismatches or desktops plugged into disabled motherboard video ports when a dedicated GPU is installed.
learning_content.technical_principle: When a discrete PCIe GPU is installed, most motherboards automatically disable integrated graphics ports by default. Checking the monitor's On-Screen Display (OSD) also proves whether the monitor panel and backlight are functional.
learning_content.limitations: A working OSD menu proves the monitor has power, but does not rule out a bad video cable or a computer failing POST.

outcomes.label: Correcting the input source, cable, or GPU port restored the display
outcomes.finding_hint: Display cable seating, wrong monitor input source, or wrong video port caused the blank screen.

transition.summary: Display restored after correcting monitor/cable configuration.

outcomes.label: Monitor powers on and shows 'No Signal', even on the correct input and port
outcomes.finding_hint: Monitor is functional, but receives no video signal from the computer.

transition.summary: Proceed to test with an alternate cable/display and minimal peripherals.

outcomes.label: Monitor shows no power LED and no OSD menu even on a known-good wall outlet
rules_out: Computer video output fault (unverified until monitor replaced)
outcomes.finding_hint: Evidence-supported monitor power or hardware failure.

transition.summary: Test with a spare monitor or escalate for monitor replacement/repair.

inconclusive.summary: Confirm whether the monitor displays an On-Screen Display (OSD) menu or 'No Signal' message.

not_performed.summary: Workflow paused pending monitor and cable check.

unable_to_perform.summary: Unable to inspect monitor connections; escalate to on-site IT support.

steps.title: Isolate Video Cable, Alternate Display, and External Peripherals
steps.objective: Rule out a defective display cable, faulty video port, or a hung boot caused by an external USB device.
instructions: Power off the computer safely by holding the power button for 5 seconds.
Disconnect all non-essential external peripherals (USB hubs, external drives, docks, printers), leaving only power and display connected.
If available, swap to a known-good video cable or connect to an alternate monitor/TV (for laptops, test an external monitor via HDMI/USB-C).
Power the system back on and observe whether any image appears (also test Caps Lock LED response on the keyboard).
steps.expected_results: Display output appears on the known-good cable/monitor or after removing conflicting USB peripherals.
safety_requirements: Power off the device before disconnecting docking stations or swapping display cables.
Do not open the computer case to reseat RAM or GPU unless trained in ESD-safe hardware service and the system is fully unplugged.

learning_content.why_this_step: Component isolation (known-good substitution) is a core IT troubleshooting principle. Testing a laptop on an external monitor also separates a failed built-in LCD panel from a motherboard/GPU failure.
learning_content.technical_principle: If Caps Lock toggles on the keyboard and an external monitor works on a laptop, the OS/motherboard is running and the fault is isolated to the built-in LCD panel or ribbon cable. If no display works on any port, the fault lies in POST (RAM, GPU, CPU, or motherboard).
learning_content.limitations: Internal component isolation (such as reseating RAM sticks or testing a discrete GPU) requires ESD precautions and powered-off internal access, so it is safely escalated.

outcomes.label: Display works with a different cable/monitor or after removing external USB devices
outcomes.finding_hint: Evidence-supported fault isolated to original display cable, built-in laptop panel, or conflicting external peripheral.

transition.summary: Fault isolated via known-good substitution. Replace the faulty cable/panel or reconnect peripherals one by one.

outcomes.label: Still no display on known-good cable/monitor with minimal peripherals connected
rules_out: Display cable or external USB peripheral conflict
outcomes.finding_hint: Evidence-supported internal No-POST / No-Video fault (suspected RAM seating, discrete GPU, or motherboard failure).

transition.summary: Escalate to L2 Hardware Technician for ESD-safe internal diagnostics (RAM reseating, CMOS reset, GPU testing) after full power disconnection.

inconclusive.summary: Note whether a spare cable/monitor was available and whether the Caps Lock LED responds.

unable_to_perform.summary: No spare cable/display available for isolation; escalate to on-site L2 Support.
